dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an m-by-n real matrix A and vector x indexed by Fin n, this is the matrix-vector product A x, whose i-th component is the finite sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j) times x(j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the maps represented by Y, ΔY, and their pointwise sum; the conclusion asserts injectivity of the map x ↦ (Y + ΔY)x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef002 A c states that for every real n-vector x, c times the Euclidean norm of x is at most the Euclidean norm of A x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to Y and μ, it supplies the global lower bound μ‖x‖₂ ≤ ‖Yx‖₂ for every x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef003 A c states that for every real n-vector x, the Euclidean norm of A x is at most c times the Euclidean norm of x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to ΔY and η, it supplies the global upper bound ‖ΔYx‖₂ ≤ η‖x‖₂ for every x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real vector x indexed by Fin n, this is the square root of the sum over all coordinates i of x(i) squared, namely its Euclidean 2-norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the domain and codomain norms in both quantitative hypotheses, instantiated at dimensions n and m as appropriate.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin k is the finite index type with elements corresponding to the natural numbers strictly below k.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fin m indexes matrix rows and output coordinates, while Fin n indexes columns and input coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: Function.Injective
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function f is injective when, for all inputs a₁ and a₂, equality f(a₁) = f(a₂) implies a₁ = a₂.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the exact conclusion required of the perturbed matrix-vector map from real n-vectors to real m-vectors.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the heterogeneous addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real-number instance, it combines Y(i,j) and ΔY(i,j) by ordinary real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the strict-order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real LT instance, it expresses the strict hypothesis η < μ.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified dimensions m and n are natural numbers, and the exponent used in the norm is the natural number 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All matrix entries, vector coordinates, bounds, products, sums, orders, and square roots in the proposition are over the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the ordinary addition operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the entrywise expression Y(i,j) + ΔY(i,j) ordinary exact real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the ordinary strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives η < μ its standard real-order meaning.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given an addition operation on a type, this constructs the corresponding homogeneous HAdd operation by using that same addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HAdd.hAdd in the perturbed entries to Real.instAdd, so the operation is real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides a finite enumeration of every element of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits the matrix products and squared-coordinate norms to be expressed as finite sums over all relevant row or column indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forms the finite sum of a function over a finite set using the supplied commutative additive monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It computes matrix-vector product coordinates and the sums of coordinate squares used by the Euclidean norms.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, Finset.univ is the finite set containing all elements of that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each sum range over every coordinate in Fin n or Fin m, rather than over a proper subset.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the heterogeneous multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real multiplication, it forms matrix-entry times vector-coordinate products and the scalar products μ‖x‖₂ and η‖x‖₂.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real LE instance, it expresses both norm inequalities using the ordinary relation ≤.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the commutative additive monoid structure of the real numbers, including real addition and zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the algebraic structure used to evaluate all finite real sums, including empty sums as zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the ordinary non-strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the lower and upper norm bounds their standard real inequality meanings.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary multiplication on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies multiplication in matrix-vector products and in multiplication of the norms by μ or η.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a multiplication operation on a type, this constructs the corresponding homogeneous HMul operation using that multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HMul.hMul to Real.instMul, making all displayed products ordinary real products.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms x(i) raised to the natural-number exponent 2 in the norm definition.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: A monoid supplies natural-number powers by repeated monoid multiplication, with exponent zero giving the identity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real numbers it interprets x(i)^2 as the ordinary square x(i)·x(i).

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the interpretation of a natural-number numeral in a type from the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the numeral 2 used as the exponent in each squared coordinate.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the multiplicative monoid structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It enables natural powers of real coordinates and therefore the exact squares appearing in the Euclidean norm.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This returns the nonnegative real square root through the nonnegative-real square-root construction; on the nonnegative sum of squares used here it is the ordinary nonnegative square root.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns each finite sum of coordinate squares into the Euclidean 2-norm used in the hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a power operation with exponent type β, this constructs the corresponding HPow operation with output in the base type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HPow.hPow on real coordinates and natural exponents to the real natural-power operation.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number numeral n as that same element n of Nat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the exponent written as 2 is exactly the natural number two.

binders: Universally quantify natural-number dimensions m and n; both may be zero.
Universally quantify real matrices Y and ΔY, each represented as a function Fin m → Fin n → Real.
Universally quantify real constants μ and η.
Each norm-bound hypothesis universally quantifies a real vector x : Fin n → Real.
The injectivity conclusion universally quantifies two real vectors x₁, x₂ : Fin n → Real.
hypotheses: For every x in R^n, μ‖x‖₂ ≤ ‖Yx‖₂.
For every x in R^n, ‖ΔYx‖₂ ≤ η‖x‖₂.
η < μ in the strict real order.
conclusions: The map from R^n to R^m given by x ↦ (Y + ΔY)x is injective.
Explicitly, for all x₁ and x₂, if for every row i the sums Σ_j (Y(i,j) + ΔY(i,j))x₁(j) and Σ_j (Y(i,j) + ΔY(i,j))x₂(j) are equal, then x₁ = x₂.
mathematical_definitions: A matrix A : Fin m → Fin n → Real acts on x by (Ax)(i) = Σ_{j in Fin n} A(i,j)x(j).
For x : Fin k → Real, ‖x‖₂ = sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin k} x(i)^2).
The perturbed matrix has entries (Y + ΔY)(i,j) = Y(i,j) + ΔY(i,j), using exact real addition.
Injectivity means that equality of the two output functions implies equality of the two input functions.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary finite dimensions m and n, let Y and ΔY be real m-by-n matrices. Suppose Y has the global lower Euclidean-norm bound μ‖x‖₂ ≤ ‖Yx‖₂ for every real n-vector x, while ΔY has the global upper Euclidean-norm bound ‖ΔYx‖₂ ≤ η‖x‖₂ for every x. If η is strictly smaller than μ, then the exact real matrix Y + ΔY defines an injective map from R^n to R^m.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition concerns finite real matrices and exact real arithmetic; it encodes no floating-point format, rounding operation, computed approximation, or roundoff error.
The norm is specifically the Euclidean 2-norm defined by a square root of a finite sum of exact squares.
The dimensions m and n are unrestricted natural numbers, so zero-dimensional cases are included.

If n = 0, the domain contains only the empty vector. Both norm hypotheses reduce to 0 ≤ 0 regardless of μ and η, and the conclusion is automatically true because every function from a singleton domain is injective.

If m = 0 and n > 0, the three hypotheses are inconsistent: the perturbation bound forces η ≥ 0, strictness gives μ > 0, and the lower bound for Y would require μ‖x‖₂ ≤ 0 for every nonzero x. Thus this dimension case is vacuous.
No nonnegativity assumptions on μ or η are stated explicitly. When n > 0, the perturbation bound forces η ≥ 0, and η < μ consequently forces μ > 0.
The constants μ and η are only lower and upper bounds. The proposition does not assert that they are optimal, attained, singular values, or exact operator norms.

The matrix need not be square. Only injectivity is concluded; surjectivity, invertibility as a square matrix, rank equality, determinant bounds, and a quantitative lower bound for Y + ΔY are not stated.
All inequalities quantify over every vector x, with no separate unit-vector restriction or normalization assumption.
